children: Debt tied to cloud-computing provider CoreWeave
plunged to all-time lows on Tuesday, leading corporate bond losses as mounting skepticism over the staying power of the AI boom spilled into the broader hyperscaler credit market.
The sell-off erased a brief Monday rebound sparked by news that Nvidia's
board had reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer. All four of CoreWeave’s
major notes had tumbled to their weakest levels since issuance in afternoon trading, Bloomberg reported, citing Trace data.

9.625% notes due July 2032 dropped as much as 4.6 points to 74.9 cents on the dollar, hitting a record low since launching in June 2026. Its 9.75% notes due October 2031 fell 3.75 points to 76.3 cents, marking their lowest price since their April debut.

Meanwhile, the company's 9% bonds due February 2031 declined as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents, breaching their previous floor set after their July 2025 issuance, while its 9.25% bonds due June 2030 slid 3 points to 80.9 cents, a low not seen since May 2025.
